# Independent audit: pure-base binding, active own sections, and vertex plateaus

Source: `candidate 5f79e6103cd27dac`, Sections 1, 3, and 5. Verdict: **PASS** under the displayed positive-fiber, actual-compatibility, interior-mark and positive-definite-covariance hypotheses.

## Whole-fiber capture and the exact gap

If an ambient closed cap contains K_p entirely, choose a strictly missed point from every not-wholly-captured fiber. An anchored combination with base p would be a strictly missed point of K_p. Actual compatibility therefore excludes p from the convex hull of those bases. Strict base separation then retains p and only wholly captured fibers, proving the claimed atomic-depth lower bound. Both the strictness of the missed points and the closed boundary convention are correct.

For delta<R(p,y), a covariance-unit normal omits positive own volume. An atomic minimizing cap can be taken through p: move its containing boundary to p, which cannot increase its mass. Finite large integer tilt fixes all nonzero base-sign fibers; zero-sign fibers are at most wholly captured and the own one loses positive volume. This gives strict mixed mass below the atomic value. For delta>=R every directional buffered own cap is full by norm duality, and the capture lemma gives equality. Rank zero reduces directly to the own fiber.

The further implication that every active cap is own-proper uses the exact gap, not a stronger global all-directions properness hypothesis. Empty own cuts are excluded because the threshold is strictly below its value at the interior source.

## Compact active representatives and coareas

The tilt-compression argument keeps all prescribed proper-fiber base drifts and full/empty inequalities. Their coefficient matrices use the fixed finite vectors z−p. Bounded right sides and the finitely many fixed active-set matrices yield bounded minimum-norm representatives; support-face traces cause no problem because only the volume status needs to be preserved. The nonzero continuous normals lie on a compact covariance-unit sphere.

A full-own limit of active representatives contradicts the strict atomic gap. An empty-own limit contradicts the uniformly interior source and positive threshold displacement. Interior section continuity then gives a positive own coarea uniformly over the compact active set. This is valid for nonsmooth bodies; no supporting-section continuity was used. Other fibers can still have supporting facets, as the source explicitly states.

Uniformization over all maximizing marks additionally uses the established own-boundary zero-depth theorem: because the buffer vanishes there, positive maximizing marks stay in a compact interior set. The stated finite continuation package follows with its existing nonsmooth supporting selectors; it does not assert full differentiability.

## Exposed-vertex plateau contraction

Nested contraction of a vertex fiber is genuinely feasible: no nontrivial anchored representation has that vertex as its target, and every representation using it as an input only becomes smaller. Thus the exact integer fibers of their convex hull are the prescribed contracted/unchanged bodies.

Each selected pure-base-bound vertex has V_p=Q. After common ratio r=(1−t)^d contraction, the singleton pure-base cap bounds every new point there by rQ, independently of the new energy and covariance. The fixed positive multiplier may be rescaled by the displayed continuous geometric-mean factor. The finitely many outside bases keep their old strict depth gap for small t by the proved all-direction slab continuity. Consequently Q(t)<=rQ and the ratio strictly decreases when any outside mass remains.

If all bases are maximizing vertices, completeness makes their parities distinct: an equal-parity midpoint would be another base that is not extreme. Equal masses then give beta=1/k, above the target. This fully solves only the stated all-vertex atomic-plateau case. The note correctly leaves interior pure-base plateaus and mixtures with other groups separate.
